Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

zuint 0.0.0.9000

  • int64(), uint64(), int128() and uint128() create signed and unsigned 64- and 128-bit integer vectors from logical, integer, double, decimal character, bit64 integer64 and each other. Conversion is exact or gives NA with a zuint_cast_warning; it never rounds or clamps.
  • int64 has class c("zu_int64", "integer64") and bit64’s storage, so code that reads integer64 reads it unchanged.
  • NA_int64_, NA_uint64_, NA_int128_ and NA_uint128_.
  • The base vector protocol for all four types: subsetting and assignment (with exact casting of the assigned value), c(), rep(), rev(), length<-, is.na(), anyNA(), as.character(), as.double() (with a zuint_precision_warning when it rounds), as.integer(), as.logical(), as.list(), data frame columns, format(), print(), str() and summary().
  • Exact arithmetic: +, -, *, %/% (floor), %% (sign of the divisor), ^ with a non-negative integer exponent, unary minus, abs() and sign(). An out-of-range result is NA with one zuint_overflow_warning per call. / and other Math functions compute in double.
  • checked_add(), checked_sub(), checked_mul(), checked_pow() and checked_neg() raise a zuint_overflow_error instead, and checked_idiv() and checked_mod() a zuint_division_error on a zero divisor; wrapping_add(), wrapping_sub(), wrapping_mul(), wrapping_pow() and wrapping_neg() compute modulo 2^64 or 2^128.
  • Mixed types follow a lossless promotion order (zu_common_type()), in arithmetic and in c(). A double must be integral and in range, unless options(zuint.double = "allow").
  • Comparison is exact across all types and doubles: int64(1) == 1.5 is FALSE, and nothing is compared through double.
  • The constructors read 0x hex and 0b binary as well as decimal, with an optional sign, _ between digits and surrounding whitespace; "NA" and blank strings are NA. Exponents are not accepted.
  • format_hex() and format_bin(), with pad = TRUE for the full width; format() takes width and big.mark; print() stops at getOption("max.print").
  • Bit operations: bit_and(), bit_or(), bit_xor(), bit_not(), shift_left(), shift_right(), popcount(), clz() and ctz().
  • With zuarrow installed, zuint registers its four types with zuarrow’s registry, so zuarrow::arrow_to_r(), zuarrow::arrow_read() and zuarrow::arrow_array() read and write int64, uint64 and DuckDB’s arrow.opaque hugeint/uhugeint exactly (?zuint-arrow). A value equal to a type’s NA bit pattern follows zuarrow’s lossy policy: an error by default, NA with a warning under lossy = "warn".
  • The Arrow and DuckDB functions of the development versions are gone, each replaced by zuarrow:
    • zu_from_arrow() and zu_to_arrow(): zuarrow::arrow_to_r() and zuarrow::arrow_array(). decimal128(p, 0) reads as int128 with to = int128(); the decimal = TRUE export has no replacement.
    • zu_sentinel_check(): the zuarrow_lossy_error that zuarrow::arrow_to_r() raises.
    • zu_duckdb_query(): zuarrow::arrow_to_r(DBI::dbGetQueryArrow(con, sql)) after SET arrow_lossless_conversion = true.
    • zu_duckdb_register(), zu_arrow_table() and zu_from_arrow_table(): zuarrow::arrow_stream(), zuarrow::arrow_write() and zuarrow::arrow_read().
    • The nanoarrow methods (convert_array(), as_nanoarrow_array(), infer_nanoarrow_schema()) and the arrow methods (as_arrow_array(), infer_type()): zuarrow, which reads and writes nanoarrow handles.
  • zu_storage() and zu_from_storage() document the payload shapes and NA bit patterns as the public representation contract.
  • as_integer64() returns a plain bit64 integer64.
  • sort(), and base order() and rank() through an exact xtfrm(), with a stable radix sort; unique(), duplicated() and anyDuplicated() with an exact hash; match(), %in% and table() compare exact values, and zu_match() and %zin% do it faster.
  • sum() is type stable and exact, NA with a warning when the total does not fit; prod(), cumsum(), cumprod(), cummax() and cummin(); min(), max() and range() are exact; mean() and median() are doubles from the exact values; diff() and seq_zu().
  • summary() adds the median and the mean.
  • rep() of an empty vector pads with the type’s NA (#55); range() takes finite, which drops NA (#56); under options(zuint.double = "allow"), sum(), prod(), min(), max() and range() give base R’s double answer (#60); zu_match() and %zin% treat a value the common type cannot hold as no match, as match() does (#58); seq_zu() counts in the elements’ own type, so it reaches the top of the unsigned ranges (#59).
  • The Arrow import refuses a schema whose format is not the array’s own (zuint_arrow_error), which would have read past the data (#61).
  • A C table for other packages, zuint_api_v1 in inst/include/zuint.h, resolved through zuint-r.h: DuckDB’s fixed-point DECIMAL(p, s) on a 128-bit coefficient (parse, format, rescale, compare, and conversion to and from double, each as DuckDB 2.0.1 does it, with two of DuckDB’s bugs fixed), and checked 128-bit arithmetic. zuint.h includes no R header, and every member is safe on any thread (#103).
  • decimal128() holds DuckDB’s DECIMAL(p, s) exactly, with is_decimal128(), decimal_precision() and decimal_scale(). +, -, *, round(), floor(), ceiling(), trunc(), cumsum(), c(), x[i] <- value and vctrs give DuckDB’s result types, and only decimal128() rounds a value into one; comparison is exact across scales and with any integer or double; match(), %in% and zu_match() find equal values whatever their scales; /, mean() and the other Math functions give doubles; and sorting, hashing, sum(), min() and max() work on the coefficients (#104, #108 to #129).
  • With vctrs, dplyr and tibble: zuint columns combine by the promotion order, cast exactly, arrange, group, summarise, bind and print. data.table keys on int64 natively.
  • zu_ifelse() and zu_vapply() keep the type where ifelse() and vapply() would read raw bits. unique() drops names, as base R’s does.
  • A getting-started vignette, and benchmarks against bit64 in the README.
  • mean() and median() of every type, decimals included, are the exact mean rounded once to the nearest double; they had rounded the sum first, so a mean could lie above max() (#148).
  • DuckDB’s arrow.opaque extension is recognised by reading its JSON as DuckDB does: the top-level vendor_name must be "DuckDB" and the top-level type_name "hugeint" or "uhugeint", escapes decoded. Another vendor’s type, or a type_name nested deeper, no longer reads as int128, and DuckDB’s own metadata with the keys in another order or written with escapes no longer reads as raw bytes. A decimal under any other arrow.opaque type no longer reads as int128 (#154).
  • to = int64() and to = uint64() read 8-, 16- and 32-bit integer columns exactly: -2147483648 had been lost as R’s NA_integer_ (#155).
  • The Arrow decimal format d:P,S is read in the specification’s form only: a precision or scale past INT_MAX no longer wraps into range, and signs and spaces are refused (#156).
  • Errors about an Arrow schema are zuint_arrow_error, and a schema with more than 4096 metadata entries is one too, where a DuckDB HUGEINT column had silently read as raw bytes (#166).
  • A plain bit64 integer64 operand is read by its values when bit64 is not loaded: in &, | and xor(), zu_match() and %zin%, zu_ifelse()’s test, checked_idiv() and checked_mod(), seq_zu()’s by, round()’s digits, comparisons and & with a decimal128, and vctrs casts to every zuint type. Base R had read its bits, where -1 is NA and NA is a value (#150).
  • With bit64 attached, integer64 * uint64, /, ^ and assigning a uint64 into an integer64 are exact: bit64 had computed on the uint64’s bits (#151).
  • Conj(), Re(), Im(), Mod() and Arg() are a zuint_unsupported_error for every type, where they had computed on the payload and kept the class (#152).
  • A zuint or integer64 count is read as the number it stands for, as an index is: rep()’s times, each and length.out, diff()’s lag and differences, head() and tail(), length<-, seq_zu()’s and seq()’s length.out, and format()’s width, print()’s max and str()’s vec.len (#153).
  • %*%, and from R 4.4.0 crossprod() and tcrossprod(), are a zuint_unsupported_error for every type, with or without bit64; for int64 the answer had depended on whether bit64 was loaded. matrix(), array(), outer() and diag() cannot be intercepted, as ?zu_ifelse says (#160).
  • With bit64 attached, its setdiff(), union(), intersect(), is.element() and setequal() work on int64: zuint declares zu_int64 a subclass of integer64 for methods::as() (#161).
  • abs(), sign(), the other Math functions computed in double, !, &, | and the double fallback of options(zuint.double = "allow") in arithmetic, ^ and c() keep names, as base R does (#164).
